kept.claim: isTeamAdminOrOwner combines isTeamAdmin && isTeamOwner, so team ADMINs (non-owners) are rejected with FORBIDDEN; only OWNERs pass.
kept.body:
## [ISSUE] `isTeamAdmin && isTeamOwner` locks team admins out

**Severity:** HIGH — team admins cannot add guests to their team's bookings; the variable name promises "admin OR owner".

### The Problem
```ts
const isTeamAdminOrOwner =
  (await isTeamAdmin(user.id, booking.eventType?.teamId ?? 0)) &&
  (await isTeamOwner(user.id, booking.eventType?.teamId ?? 0));
```

### Theory / Proof
`packages/lib/server/queries/teams/index.ts:264-284` — `isTeamAdmin` already matches `OR: [{ role: "ADMIN" }, { role: "OWNER" }]`. `isTeamOwner` (`:286-295`) matches only `role: "OWNER"`. ANDing them reduces the check to "is OWNER". A member with role `ADMIN` gets `isTeamAdmin` truthy and `isTeamOwner` false, so `isTeamAdminOrOwner === false`, and unless they are also the organizer/attendee they hit `FORBIDDEN` at line 54.

### What happens today vs. what will break
Owners work; admins managing a round-robin/collective booking hosted by another member get `you_do_not_have_permission`.

### Research
Elsewhere in the codebase `isTeamAdmin` alone is used as the admin-or-owner check (it returns the membership for either role).

### Recommendation
```ts
const teamId = booking.eventType?.teamId;
const isTeamAdminOrOwner = teamId ? !!(await isTeamAdmin(user.id, teamId)) : false;
```
(`isTeamAdmin` already covers OWNER; also avoid querying `teamId: 0`.)
kept.evidence: addGuests.handler.ts:46-48 ANDs isTeamAdmin with isTeamOwner; teams/index.ts:264-284 shows isTeamAdmin already matches ADMIN or OWNER, and isTeamOwner (286-295) matches only OWNER, so the check passes only for owners. A non-organizer, non-attendee ADMIN gets FORBIDDEN at 54-55.

kept.claim: Attendee access is intentional, but the handler does not respect the event type's guests booking field (hidden/disabled). An attendee who has a Cal.com account can add guests and trigger organizer-branded invite emails even when the organizer disabled guests for that event type, and nothing caps or rate-limits this.
kept.body:
## [GAP ANALYSIS] Attendees can add guests even when the event type hides/disables the guests field

**Severity:** MEDIUM — the organizer's "no guests" setting for an event type can be bypassed after booking, and every call sends organizer-branded invites.

### The Problem
```ts
const isAttendee = !!booking.attendees.find((attendee) => attendee.email === user.email);
if (!isTeamAdminOrOwner && !isOrganizer && !isAttendee) { throw ... }
```
Letting attendees in looks intentional. However, nothing in the handler reads `booking.eventType.bookingFields`, so if the organizer hid or disabled the `guests` booking field, an attendee with a Cal.com account can still add arbitrary guests here.

### Theory / Proof
- At booking time, guests enter only through the booking form, which respects the event type's `guests` field. This endpoint is a second entry point that skips that rule.
- Each successful call runs `sendAddGuestsEmails` (`email-manager.ts:525-550`). That sends an ICS `METHOD:REQUEST` to every attendee, with the organizer's name in `from` (`attendee-add-guests-email.ts`). The route (`_router.tsx`, `authedProcedure`) has no rate limit.

### What happens today vs. what will break
An organizer who disabled guests for an event type ("1:1 only") can still have extra people added, and invited in the organizer's name, by the booker.

### Recommendation
Enforce the event type's guest setting for non-organizer callers:
```ts
const guestsField = eventTypeBookingFields
  .parse(booking.eventType?.bookingFields ?? [])
  .find((f) => f.name === "guests");
if (isAttendee && !isOrganizer && !isTeamAdminOrOwner && guestsField?.hidden) {
  throw new TRPCError({ code: "FORBIDDEN", message: "you_do_not_have_permission" });
}
```
Consider adding a rate limit (e.g. `checkRateLimitAndThrowError` keyed on user id), as other email-sending endpoints do.
kept.evidence: Attendee access (handler:52-56) is an explicit, intentional branch, so 'attendees can add guests' is by design. What holds: the handler never reads eventType.bookingFields, so a hidden/disabled guests field is not enforced; each call sends emails via sendAddGuestsEmails (email-manager.ts:525-550), and the route has no rate limit.
kept.corrected_claim: Attendee access is intentional, but the handler does not respect the event type's guests booking field (hidden/disabled). An attendee who has a Cal.com account can add guests and trigger organizer-branded invite emails even when the organizer disabled guests for that event type, and nothing caps or rate-limits this.

kept.claim: Server schema accepts an unbounded guests array with no dedup, so duplicate emails in one request create duplicate Attendee rows and there is no cap on emails sent per call.
kept.body:
## [ISSUE] Unbounded, non-deduplicated `guests` input

**Severity:** MEDIUM — duplicate attendee rows and unbounded email fan-out per request.

### The Problem
```ts
guests: z.array(z.string().email()),
```
Uniqueness is only enforced in the client (`AddGuestsDialog.tsx` `refine`). The handler's `uniqueGuests` filter (line 74) only removes emails already on the booking, not duplicates inside the request.

### Theory / Proof
Request `{ bookingId, guests: ["a@x.com", "a@x.com"] }`: both pass the filter, `createMany` inserts two Attendee rows (Attendee has no unique constraint on `(bookingId, email)`), and `sendAddGuestsEmails` sends two emails to that address. An array of thousands of addresses is also accepted.

### What happens today vs. what will break
Via the UI it works because the dialog dedupes. Any direct tRPC call (or a future client) bypasses this.

### Research
Zod supports `.max()` and `.refine`/`.transform` on arrays; tRPC recommends validating on the server since the client is untrusted.

### Recommendation
```ts
guests: z
  .array(z.string().email().transform((e) => e.toLowerCase()))
  .min(1)
  .max(10)
  .transform((arr) => Array.from(new Set(arr))),
```
kept.evidence: addGuests.schema.ts:5 has no .max() and no dedup; the only uniqueness check is client-side (AddGuestsDialog.tsx:26-29). The handler filter (74-78) does not dedupe within the request. The Attendee model (schema.prisma:526-539) has no unique (bookingId,email), so createMany inserts duplicates and email-manager.ts:539-546 sends one email per row.

kept.claim: Guest emails are compared case-sensitively against the lowercased blacklist and existing attendees, so 'Blocked@Spam.com' bypasses BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS and existing attendees can be re-added with different casing.
kept.evidence: handler:70-72 lowercases the blacklist, but 74-78 compare the raw guest (includes / ===), and neither the zod schema nor the dialog normalises case. handleNewBooking.ts:736-744 correctly compares extractBaseEmail(guest).toLowerCase().

kept.claim: sendAddGuestsEmails ignores the event type's disableStandardEmails metadata (eventTypeDisableHostEmail / eventTypeDisableAttendeeEmail), unlike sendLocationChangeEmails right above it.
kept.evidence: email-manager.ts:525-548 takes no eventTypeMetadata and sends unconditionally. The sibling sendLocationChangeEmails (495-523) and almost all other senders check eventTypeDisableHostEmail/AttendeeEmail (81-87). The handler loads eventType (line 32) but does not pass its metadata (line 168).

kept.claim: evt omits iCalUID/iCalSequence, so the REQUEST ICS uses booking.uid as UID while the original invite used `${uid}@Cal.com`; recipients' calendar clients create a duplicate event instead of updating the existing one.
kept.body:
## [ISSUE] ICS update uses a different UID than the original invite

**Severity:** MEDIUM — existing attendees get a second copy of the meeting in their calendar instead of an update.

### The Problem
```ts
const evt: CalendarEvent = {
  ...
  uid: booking.uid,
  // no iCalUID, no iCalSequence
```
`generateIcsString` uses `uid: event.iCalUID || event.uid!` and `sequence: event.iCalSequence || 0`.

### Theory / Proof
New bookings store `iCalUID = getICalUID({ uid })` which is `${uid}@${APP_NAME}` (`packages/emails/lib/getICalUID.ts`, `handleNewBooking.ts:829`). The original confirmation ICS therefore has `UID:<uid>@Cal.com`. The add-guests ICS (`attendee-add-guests-email.ts`, `method: "REQUEST"`) has `UID:<uid>`. RFC 5545 §3.8.4.7: UID identifies the component; RFC 5546 §3.2.2: a REQUEST with a new UID is a new event, not an update. `booking.iCalUID`/`iCalSequence` are selected by the `findFirst` include but never copied into `evt`. `requestReschedule.handler.ts:199` shows the correct pattern (`iCalUID: bookingToReschedule.iCalUID`).

### What happens today vs. what will break
Gmail/Outlook/Apple Calendar key events by UID. Existing attendees who accepted the first invite see a second event at the same time.

### Recommendation
```ts
const evt: CalendarEvent = {
  ...
  uid: booking.uid,
  iCalUID: booking.iCalUID,
  iCalSequence: (booking.iCalSequence ?? 0) + 1,
```
kept.evidence: handler:124-147 never sets iCalUID or iCalSequence, although include loads both (schema.prisma:592-593). generateIcsString falls back to event.uid and sequence 0. handleNewBooking.ts:829-832 stores `${uid}@${APP_NAME}` (getICalUID.ts:30), so the REQUEST ICS UID does not match the original invite.

kept.claim: The handler does not reject CANCELLED/REJECTED bookings, so an authorized user (organizer, attendee or team admin) calling the API directly can add guests to a cancelled booking. Those guests then get a REQUEST ICS with status CONFIRMED. The past-booking part is not a gap, because the UI deliberately offers Add Guests on past confirmed bookings.
kept.body:
## [GAP ANALYSIS] Guests can be added to cancelled/rejected bookings

**Severity:** MEDIUM — new guests get a CONFIRMED meeting invite for a meeting that was cancelled.

### The Problem
After `if (!booking) throw ...` the handler goes straight to permission checks and `booking.update`. There is no check on `booking.status`.

### Theory / Proof
The route is a plain `authedProcedure`, callable directly with any `bookingId` the caller can access (organizer, attendee, team owner). For a `CANCELLED` or `REJECTED` booking, the handler inserts the attendees and sends emails built in `attendee-add-guests-email.ts` / `organizer-add-guests-email.ts`. Those hard-code `status: "CONFIRMED"` and `method: "REQUEST"`, so every recipient's calendar treats the cancelled meeting as confirmed.

### Recommendation
```ts
if (booking.status === BookingStatus.CANCELLED || booking.status === BookingStatus.REJECTED) {
  throw new TRPCError({ code: "BAD_REQUEST", message: "booking_is_cancelled" });
}
```
kept.evidence: handler:44-56 has no booking.status check before createMany (92-106) and the CONFIRMED/REQUEST emails; a plain authedProcedure makes it directly callable. The past-booking part was disputed: the validator reported that the UI deliberately exposes edit actions for some past bookings, so it is not treated as a gap.
kept.corrected_claim: The handler does not reject CANCELLED/REJECTED bookings, so an authorized user (organizer, attendee or team admin) calling the API directly can add guests to a cancelled booking. Those guests then get a REQUEST ICS with status CONFIRMED. The past-booking part is not a gap, because the UI deliberately offers Add Guests on past confirmed bookings.

kept.claim: sendAddGuestsEmails is passed the raw `guests` input instead of `uniqueGuests`, so an existing attendee resubmitted in the list gets a fresh 'scheduled' email instead of the 'guests added' update.
kept.body:
## [ISSUE] Email routing uses unfiltered `guests` instead of `uniqueGuests`

**Severity:** LOW — wrong email template for existing attendees who appear in the input.

### The Problem
```ts
await sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests);
```
In `email-manager.ts:541`, `newGuests.includes(attendee.email)` decides between `AttendeeScheduledEmail` (new booking confirmation) and `AttendeeAddGuestsEmail` (update).

### Theory / Proof
If the request is `["existing@x.com", "new@x.com"]` where `existing@x.com` is already an attendee, `uniqueGuests` correctly drops it from the insert, but `guests` still contains it, so the existing attendee is sent a new "booking scheduled" email instead of the "new guests added" update.

### Recommendation
```ts
await sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, uniqueGuests);
```
kept.evidence: handler:74-78 filters existing attendees into uniqueGuests, but line 168 passes the raw guests. email-manager.ts sendAddGuestsEmails picks AttendeeScheduledEmail when newGuests.includes(email), so an existing attendee who is resubmitted gets the 'scheduled' email.
